classification.difficultyReason: Choose a useful regular-hexagon decomposition and connect the midpoint construction to triangle heights or corner areas to obtain an exact area fraction.

content.prompt: In the regular hexagon pictured below, the midpoints of adjacent sides are joined to form a smaller regular hexagon (shaded below). What fraction of the larger hexagon is shaded?

spec.description: Outer regular hexagon with horizontal top and bottom sides; the shaded inner hexagon joins consecutive side midpoints and has vertical left and right sides. The six corner triangles remain unshaded.
spec.mathematics: The smaller hexagon consists exactly of the six consecutive midpoint segments.
spec.answerVisibility: The requested region is shaded; no area fraction is supplied.

answer.short:
$\dfrac34$.

Partition each hexagon into six equilateral triangles and compare their areas.
answer.worked:
Let the smaller and larger hexagons have side lengths $x$ and $y$. Each splits into six equilateral triangles, so
$$\begin{align*}A_{\text{small}}&=6\left(\frac{\sqrt3x^2}{4}\right)\\A_{\text{small}}&=\frac{3\sqrt3x^2}{2},\\A_{\text{large}}&=6\left(\frac{\sqrt3y^2}{4}\right)\\A_{\text{large}}&=\frac{3\sqrt3y^2}{2}.\end{align*}$$
A side of the smaller hexagon equals the perpendicular height of one of the larger hexagon's equilateral triangles. Hence
$$\begin{align*}x^2&=y^2-\left(\frac y2\right)^2\\x^2&=\frac{3y^2}{4}\\\frac{A_{\text{small}}}{A_{\text{large}}}&=\frac{x^2}{y^2}\\\frac{A_{\text{small}}}{A_{\text{large}}}&=\frac34.\end{align*}$$
